name: pay_someone
description: Station A, A2 (fix). Identical interface and scope to A1. The only change: the recipe owns the write and enforces three deterministic rules (positive amount, $500 limit, sufficient balance) before calling POST /payments, and the skill requires the customer's confirmation (the payee rule). That confirmation setting is the one documented difference the model can see: it is the fix.

input.description: Pay another Dewy Bank customer from one of the signed-in customer's own accounts. Use this when the customer asks to pay, send money to or pay back someone else. Identify the account to pay from by the name the customer sees, for example "Everyday Checking"; call list_my_accounts first if you are not sure of the exact name. Identify the person being paid by their email address; the money goes to their checking account. The amount is in US dollars. Returns a status (completed, refused or failed), a plain-language message to relay to the customer, and the account, recipient and amount involved. Add a note only if the customer asks for one; it appears on both customers' activity. If the status is refused or failed, no money was paid: explain the message to the customer instead of retrying with different values.

The account must resolve to one of the customer's accounts before anything else happens.

FIX (Station A, Factor II): the recipe owns the write. Each rule below is a deterministic step that does not depend on the model or the prompt. Rule 1: the amount must be positive. The payee rule is the skill's confirmation: the customer approves every payment before this recipe runs.
FIX rule 2: per-payment limit of 500 US dollars.
FIX rule 3: the account paid from must cover the amount.
